meta.title: MODIS and VIIRS Harmonization
meta.description: Harmonized MODIS and VIIRS hotspot series (NASA FIRMS) for Latin America: map, burn calendar and period comparison.

footer.notice: Values are harmonized estimates derived from satellite observations: a hotspot is not a confirmed fire, and no detections does not prove there was no fire.
footer.credit: Hotspot data: NASA FIRMS (MODIS C6.1 and VIIRS C2 375 m). Basemap: OpenFreeMap, © OpenStreetMap contributors.

home.title: MODIS and VIIRS Harmonization · Latam focused system
home.lead: A pipeline calibrates NASA FIRMS hotspots so MODIS years and VIIRS years can be compared. {years} years of series, explored on a map, a burn calendar and month-to-month comparisons.

problem.title: Two sensors, one series
problem.statement: VIIRS detects about four times more hotspots than MODIS. Added up without calibration, the sensor change looks like an increase in fire.
problem.imageAlt: Illustration of the two sensors, MODIS and VIIRS

gather.title: Gather
gather.body: NASA FIRMS active-fire hotspots from four satellites: Terra and Aqua (MODIS), NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 (VIIRS), normalized to a common schema.

calibrate.title: Calibrate
calibrate.body: A k factor per region and month brings VIIRS to the MODIS scale. In the NOAA-20 vs MODIS validation, bias drops from +262 % to +0.05 %.

explore.title: Explore
explore.body: H3 cells on the map, with their p05–p95 interval and coverage. Months and years are compared on the same color scale.

analysis.lead: Harmonized series of equivalent hotspots per month (MODIS Terra + Aqua scale).

team.title: The team
team.lead: We built Terra Australis for the NASA Space Apps Challenge: a hotspot series that can be compared between MODIS years and VIIRS years, for people who study or manage fire in Latin America.
team.thanks: To NASA FIRMS for the MODIS and VIIRS active-fire data; to OpenFreeMap and the OpenStreetMap contributors for the basemap; and to the open projects H3, MapLibre, deck.gl and DuckDB.
team.specialBody: He contributed ideas for the design and visual identity of the app, so it also appeals to kids.

expl.title: Exploratory: biomass and CO₂
expl.warn: First-order estimate, not validated. Computing it with MODIS or with VIIRS typically changes the result ×2 and up to ×10: good for orders of magnitude, not for citing.
expl.formula: FRE = Σ days (ΣFRP of one sensor family ÷ nominal overpasses) × 86,400 s; biomass = FRE × {coef} kg/MJ (Wooster et al. 2005); CO₂ = biomass × {ef} kg/kg (Andreae 2019).
